posts.copy:
Cambricon's revenue more than doubled in the third quarter of 2026. Two smaller numbers in the same results say more than that one.

First, the headline. The Beijing chip designer reported CNY3.531 billion of quarterly revenue, up 104.47% year on year, and CNY1.404 billion of net profit, up 147.74%. Both are records since it listed in 2020. Yicai reads it as strong demand in China for homegrown chips.

Now the two smaller numbers.

Operating cash flow for the quarter was negative, at minus CNY83.68 million.

Total liabilities rose 56% from the end of June.

Read from a desk in London, that is one company's good quarter. Together, the three numbers say record profit and negative operating cash in the same three months. That gap is where the real questions sit.

A results table does not tell you who is buying, what they are building on the chips, or how long they will wait for supply. Those answers sit with the people doing the building, and you get them in the room.

The number is the headline. The buyers are the story.

If you want to see this on the ground for yourself, work with us.

DM us, or write to us at hello@oj.ventures

Source: Yicai Global, 26 October 2026: https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/cambricons-third-quarter-revenue-net-profit-both-hit-all-time-quarterly-highs-since-the-company-went-public?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=A-OJV202646-M

#China #Semiconductors #AI #DeepTech

posts.copy:
7,500. That is how many restaurants McDonald's had in mainland China by November 2025, eight years after giving up control.

In January 2017 it sold its mainland China and Hong Kong operation to a CITIC-led consortium, with Carlyle, for up to $2.08 billion. CITIC took 52%. McDonald's kept 20%. The stated plan was over 1,500 new restaurants in five years.

By late 2023 the count was 5,600, double the 2017 number. McDonald's then bought out Carlyle and went to 48%. Still a minority. CITIC kept its 52%.

When the numbers came good, McDonald's did not take the majority back. It added stake and left the controlling seat where it was.

We cannot prove the structure caused the growth. We can say McDonald's chose to keep it.

Many Western firms treat a local partner as a door opener and keep every decision at home. Across 15+ ecosystems with different rules, cultures and buyer behaviour, the better question is who decides once you are inside.

Our GTM advisory works through exactly that: which decisions stay home, which move to the market, and who holds each.

We have never worked with McDonald's. This is commentary from the outside.

If you want your APAC go-to-market to look like this, work with us.

DM us, or write to us at hello@oj.ventures

Source: China Daily HK, 22 December 2025: https://www.chinadailyhk.com/article/625871?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=B-OJV202646-W

#APAC #China #MarketEntry #GoToMarket

posts.verificationNotes: Over 7,500 mainland restaurants as of Nov 2025: China Daily HK, 22 Dec 2025. Jan 2017 deal for up to $2.08bn, CITIC 52% / Carlyle 28% / McDonald's 20%, and the plan for 1,500+ new restaurants in five years: Cleary Gottlieb, 9 Jan 2017. 5,600 restaurants, double 2017, and the stake moving from 20% to 48% with CITIC keeping 52%: Jiemian. That page carries no year; the year is fixed by Bloomberg's 21 Nov 2023 report of the same deal. McDonald's corporate release returned 403. The copy says outright that the structure is not proven to have caused the growth.
